chunks: And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Yazid al-Kunasī who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): When is it permissible for a father to marry off his daughter without consulting her? He said: 'When she has passed nine years of age. If he marries her before reaching nine years, the choice remains with her when she reaches nine years.'

And this addition I found in the book of al-Mushayyikhah from Yazid al-Kunasī: I said: 'If her father marries her and she has not yet reached nine years, and she hears of it and remains silent and does not object, is it permissible for her?' He said: 'It is not permissible for her as a consent in herself, nor is it permissible for her as an objection or displeasure in herself, until she completes nine years. And when she reaches nine years, it is permissible for her to speak for herself with consent or objection, and it becomes valid for her after that, even if she has not attained the maturity of women [in menstruation].'

I said: 'Are the legal punishments applied to her and is she taken [for marriage] in that state, while she is only nine years old and has not attained the maturity of women in menstruation?' He said: 'Yes, when she enters upon her husband and she is nine years old, the orphanhood [of being under full guardianship] leaves her, her wealth is given to her, and the complete legal punishments are applied to her and for her.'

I said: 'Does the boy follow the same ruling as the girl?' He said: 'O Abu Khalid, indeed if a boy is married by his father and he has not attained maturity, he has the choice when he attains maturity and reaches fifteen years, or grows hair on his face, or grows hair in his pubic area before that.'

I said: 'If his wife is brought to him before he attains maturity, and he stays with her as Allah wills, then later he attains maturity and dislikes her and objects to her?' He said: 'If it was his father who married him and he entered with her, enjoyed from her, and stayed with her for a year, he has no choice when he attains maturity, and it is not proper for him to return to his father what he did, and it is not permissible for him [to annul it].'

I said to him: 'If his father marries him and he enters with her while he is not yet mature, are the legal punishments applied to him while in that state?' He said: 'As for the complete punishments by which a man is taken, no. But he is lashed in all the punishments according to the extent of his age, so that is taken from him between him and fifteen years, so that the punishments of Allah in His creation do not become void, nor do the rights of the Muslims among them become void.'

I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, if he divorces her in that state and he has not yet attained maturity, is his divorce valid?' He said: 'If he touched her in the private part, then her divorce is valid for her and for him. And if he did not touch her in the private part and she did not enjoy from him, then she is separated from him and returns to her family, so he does not see her and she does not approach him until he attains maturity and is asked, and it is said to him: Indeed you divorced your wife So-and-so. If he confirms that and validates the divorce, she becomes a final divorce, and he is suitor among the suitors.'

So it does not contradict what we previously mentioned from the narrations, because he said: 'When she has passed nine years, it is permissible for the father to marry her without consulting her,' and this is what we say. Therefore, this does not indicate that before that he has no right except by the indication of the text, and the indication of the text can be turned away by another indication. And we have previously mentioned what indicates that he has the right to contract marriage for her before she reaches nine years and while she is a child.

As for what the author of al-Mushayyikhah narrated and what we mentioned from him regarding the addition, the way to reconcile it is to carry it on the meaning that what is meant by mentioning the father is the grandfather in the absence of the father. For if that is the case, the choice is hers when she reaches maturity. As for the nearest father, she has no choice with him at all without disagreement.

As for his saying (peace be upon him): 'When she has passed nine years, she has consent and objection in herself.' It is permissible that this is informing about her ruling with non-fathers, and there is not in the narration that she has that with the father or with non-fathers. And the benefit in that is that her consent and displeasure before she reaches nine years have no ruling.

And what we said that she does not have the power to annul the contract is clarified by his saying in the narration when he mentioned the ruling of the son: 'The boy, if his father marries him and he has not attained maturity, has the choice when he attains.' This indicates that the ruling of the girl is contrary to it, and she does not have the choice, and that is specific to the boy. And it is possible that what is meant by these two narrations from mentioning the father is the grandfather, if the father of the girl is dead. For if the matter is as we mentioned, it follows the same as others in that it is not contracted for her except with her consent, and whenever it is contracted for her while she is a child, the contract is suspended upon her consent at maturity.
And we will clarify later that the grandfather does not contract marriage for her in the absence of the father except with her consent, if Allah wills.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And when the mature woman contracts marriage for herself without the permission of her father, the contract is valid and the father does not have the right to annul it, whether it was due to his obstinacy or not.' What indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The choice/right to annul or confirm
key_terms.تِسْعُ سِنِينَ: Nine years (age of legal capacity for marriage consent)

ai.seo_question: At what age can a father marry off his daughter without her consent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of *kuf'* (guardianship), establishing that a father may marry off his pre-pubescent daughter without her consent, with the marriage becoming binding upon her silence after age nine. It distinguishes this from the ruling for boys, who retain the option of *khiyar* (choice) until age fifteen or the emergence of pubic hair, and notes that full legal accountability (*hudud*) begins upon consummation regardless of age. The text also addresses the grandfather's role, suggesting his guardianship may be contingent upon the daughter's consent if the father is absent, reflecting the nuanced scholarly debate on whether *kuf'* is absolute or conditional.
